best_architecture: Separate Unsloth (a fine-tuning/quantization tool) from the serving engine. Use Unsloth for 4-bit NF4/Dynamic GGUF quantization, then serve via vLLM (continuous batching, PagedAttention, OpenAI-compatible) for multi-user or llama.cpp/Ollama for single-box GGUF. Do NOT co-resident both models on 48GB — keep one brain model loaded, treat Qwen2.5-Coder-32B as swap-in fallback. For streaming: use the engine's native SSE endpoint; if calling transformers directly, bridge TextIteratorStreamer via a background Thread to a FastAPI StreamingResponse. KEY: Unsloth Dynamic quants beat naive Q4_0 for tool-call accuracy. Chat templates MUST match the model variant (apply_chat_template with tools=, correct --tool-call-parser). CRITICAL UNCERTAINTY: Gemma 3 vs Gemma 4 distinction — Gemma 3 uses pythonic tool calling; 'Gemma 4 MoE' details unverified, may be forward-dated. (Part B verification update: Gemma 4 GGUFs and a dedicated vLLM gemma4_tool_parser now exist as of mid-2026, distinct from the Gemma 3 pythonic parser — the version branch in the spec is therefore real and required.)

pitfalls: Using Unsloth as a production serving engine. Unsloth's FastLanguageModel + model.generate() has no continuous batching, no PagedAttention, and serializes requests — throughput collapses under concurrency. Unsloth is for quantization/fine-tuning; serve the resulting weights with vLLM (multi-user) or llama.cpp/Ollama (single-box GGUF).

padding-side flip bug. Unsloth silently resets tokenizer.padding_side from 'left' back to 'right' inside model.generate(), so the NEXT batched tokenization right-pads a decoder-only model and corrupts batched output (and triggers the 'right-padding was detected' warning). Set tokenizer.padding_side='left' immediately before EVERY tokenization call, not once at init. (unslothai/unsloth issues #3283, #2217, #2138, #2939). Best avoided entirely by serving via vLLM, which manages padding internally.

Double-BOS token corruption. Applying the chat template (which already prepends <bos>) AND letting the engine add BOS again yields two leading <bos> tokens, degrading quality ('Detected duplicate leading <bos> in prompt'). On Gemma this is acute: llama.cpp has hardcoded add_bos=true in some builds so --override-kv tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token=bool:false does NOT help; fix by removing bos_token from the chat template or passing add_special_tokens=False when you already templated.

Chat-template / parser mismatch between model variant and engine parser. Wrong --tool-call-parser or wrong .jinja produces empty tool_calls and raw tool-call tokens leaking into message.content. Gemma 3 needs --tool-call-parser pythonic + tool_chat_template_gemma3_pythonic.jinja; Gemma 4 needs the dedicated gemma4_tool_parser. Never reuse a Llama/Hermes parser for Gemma.

Gemma 3 vs Gemma 4 tool-call format confusion (CRITICAL). Gemma 3 emits a pythonic list e.g. [get_weather(city='SF')] parsed by the pythonic parser; Gemma 4 uses native <|tool_call> / <tool_call|> delimited calls parsed by gemma4_tool_parser. Branching on the wrong format silently drops every tool call. Detect the variant at load and pick the parser/template accordingly.

Naive Q4_0 accuracy degradation. Plain llama.cpp Q4_0/Q4_K quantization measurably hurts tool-call/structured-output accuracy versus Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 quants, which sit on the SOTA KL-divergence Pareto frontier. Always pull the unsloth/*-GGUF Dynamic build, not a generic Q4_0.

KV-cache OOM at long context. FP16 KV cache grows as 2 * layers * heads * head_dim * context * batch and is NOT shrunk by GPTQ/AWQ (those quantize weights, not the cache). On a 48GB A6000 a 32B model + long context + batch can OOM purely on KV. Cap max-model-len, set vLLM gpu-memory-utilization conservatively, and reject over-limit requests up front; optionally use FP8 KV cache (see SOTA).

asyncio deadlock / event-loop starvation. Calling blocking model.generate() directly inside an async FastAPI route freezes the event loop (health checks time out, all concurrent requests stall ~10x). Run generate() in a background Thread feeding a TextIteratorStreamer, or offload via loop.run_in_executor / Starlette run_in_threadpool. Never call future.result() from inside the loop thread — classic streaming deadlock.

GPU memory fragmentation with multiple model loads. Loading the primary then the Qwen2.5-Coder-32B fallback into the same process fragments VRAM and OOMs even when nominal totals fit. Do not co-resident; keep one brain loaded and swap (free + torch.cuda.empty_cache(), or run the fallback in a separate process/engine) before loading the other.

Assuming FP8 KV cache speeds up compute on Ampere. The A6000 (SM 8.6) supports only fp8_e5m2 KV cache and gets memory savings ONLY — no FP8 compute acceleration (that needs Hopper/Ada). fp8_e4m3 raises 'type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture'. Treat FP8 KV as a context-length win, not a latency win.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: Model loading and warmup
  Scenario: Primary brain loads once and is warmed before serving traffic
    Given the server starts with the Gemma 4 Dynamic 4-bit weights configured as primary
    When the lifespan startup hook runs
    Then the model and tokenizer are loaded exactly once into VRAM
    And tokenizer.padding_side is set to 'left'
    And a warmup generation of a short prompt completes successfully
    And the /health endpoint reports 'ready' only after warmup finishes
    And no second model is resident in VRAM at startup

Feature: Streaming token delivery without blocking the event loop
  Scenario: Tokens stream over SSE while other requests stay responsive
    Given the model is loaded and ready
    When a client POSTs a chat completion with stream=true
    Then generation runs in a background thread feeding a TextIteratorStreamer
    And each token is yielded as an SSE data frame as it is produced
    And a concurrent /health request returns within 200ms during generation
    And the stream terminates with a 'data: [DONE]' sentinel

Feature: Tool-call parsing for Gemma
  Scenario Outline: The correct parser is selected per Gemma variant
    Given the loaded model variant is <variant>
    And tools are supplied via apply_chat_template(tools=...)
    When the model emits a tool call
    Then the <parser> extracts it into structured tool_calls
    And message.content contains no raw tool-call tokens
    Examples:
      | variant | parser            |
      | gemma-3 | pythonic parser   |
      | gemma-4 | gemma4 parser     |

Feature: Fallback routing to Qwen2.5-Coder on primary failure
  Scenario: Primary failure swaps in the coder fallback without co-residency
    Given the Gemma primary is loaded and the Qwen2.5-Coder-32B fallback is NOT resident
    When a request to the primary raises a fatal generation error
    Then the router unloads the primary and calls torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    And it loads Qwen2.5-Coder-32B into the freed VRAM
    And the request is retried and answered by the fallback
    And at no point are both models resident simultaneously

Feature: KV cache OOM rejection
  Scenario: An over-budget context is rejected before allocation
    Given max_model_len is configured to fit within the 48GB KV budget
    When a request arrives whose prompt plus max_tokens exceeds max_model_len
    Then the server returns HTTP 400 with a context_length_exceeded error
    And no KV cache is allocated for the rejected request
    And in-flight generations for other clients are unaffected
optimal_implementation:
Run a FastAPI OpenAI-compatible server that loads ONE brain model at startup, streams via SSE off the event loop, branches the tool parser by Gemma variant, handles client disconnect, and enforces a hard context limit. Prefer vLLM AsyncLLMEngine for multi-user (it solves padding, batching, and KV management); the transformers+Thread path below is the single-box fallback.

=== Startup: load once, warm up ===
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, HTTPException
from sse_starlette.sse import EventSourceResponse
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TextIteratorStreamer
from threading import Thread
import torch, asyncio

STATE = {}
MODEL_VARIANT = 'gemma-4'      # detect from config/name; drives parser branch
MAX_MODEL_LEN = 8192

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('unsloth/gemma-4-... ')
    tok.padding_side = 'left'                      # set; re-set before every tokenize
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        'unsloth/gemma-4-...', load_in_4bit=True, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        device_map='cuda', attn_implementation='flash_attention_2')
    STATE['tok'], STATE['model'] = tok, model
    # warmup
    ids = tok('ping', return_tensors='pt').to('cuda')
    model.generate(**ids, max_new_tokens=1)
    STATE['ready'] = True
    yield
    STATE.clear()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

@app.get('/health')
async def health():
    return {'status': 'ready' if STATE.get('ready') else 'loading'}

=== Context-limit guard (avoid KV OOM) ===
def enforce_limit(prompt_ids, max_new):
    if prompt_ids.shape[-1] + max_new > MAX_MODEL_LEN:
        raise HTTPException(400, 'context_length_exceeded')

=== Streaming without blocking the loop ===
async def stream_tokens(messages, tools, max_new, request: Request):
    tok, model = STATE['tok'], STATE['model']
    tok.padding_side = 'left'                      # re-set: generate() resets it
    prompt = tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tools=tools,
                                     add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False)
    ids = tok(prompt, return_tensors='pt', add_special_tokens=False).to('cuda')  # add_special_tokens=False -> no double BOS
    enforce_limit(ids['input_ids'], max_new)
    streamer = TextIteratorStreamer(tok, skip_prompt=True, skip_special_tokens=True)
    gen_kwargs = dict(**ids, streamer=streamer, max_new_tokens=max_new)
    Thread(target=model.generate, kwargs=gen_kwargs, daemon=True).start()  # off the loop
    buf = []
    for piece in streamer:                         # sync iterator; yield cooperatively
        if await request.is_disconnected():        # client disconnect -> stop work
            break
        buf.append(piece)
        yield {'event': 'message', 'data': piece}
        await asyncio.sleep(0)                      # let the loop breathe
    calls = parse_tool_calls(''.join(buf), MODEL_VARIANT)
    if calls:
        yield {'event': 'tool_calls', 'data': json.dumps(calls)}
    yield {'event': 'done', 'data': '[DONE]'}

=== Version-branched tool-call parser (Gemma 3 pythonic vs Gemma 4) ===
import ast, re, json
def parse_tool_calls(text, variant):
    if variant.startswith('gemma-3'):
        # pythonic: [fn(arg='x'), ...]
        m = re.search(r'\[.*\]', text, re.S)
        if not m: return []
        node = ast.parse(m.group(0), mode='eval').body
        out = []
        for call in getattr(node, 'elts', []):
            out.append({'name': call.func.id,
                        'arguments': {kw.arg: ast.literal_eval(kw.value) for kw in call.keywords}})
        return out
    else:  # gemma-4: <|tool_call> {json} <tool_call|> delimited
        out = []
        for m in re.finditer(r'<\|tool_call\|?>(.*?)<\|?tool_call\|>', text, re.S):
            try: out.append(json.loads(m.group(1)))
            except json.JSONDecodeError: pass
        return out

@app.post('/v1/chat/completions')
async def chat(req: Request):
    body = await req.json()
    if not STATE.get('ready'): raise HTTPException(503, 'loading')
    return EventSourceResponse(stream_tokens(body['messages'], body.get('tools'),
                                             body.get('max_tokens', 512), req))

=== Fallback routing (no co-residency) ===

# load Qwen2.5-Coder-32B into the freed VRAM, retry. Never load both at once.

PRODUCTION NOTE: replace the transformers+Thread core with vLLM:
  vllm serve unsloth/gemma-4-... --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
       --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --dtype bfloat16
(for Gemma 3 use --tool-call-parser pythonic --chat-template tool_chat_template_gemma3_pythonic.jinja). vLLM then provides the OpenAI API, continuous batching, PagedAttention, native SSE, and correct padding/BOS handling, so the custom server above is only needed for the single-box GGUF/transformers path.
sota_improvements: vLLM continuous batching vs HF generate: PagedAttention + continuous batching gives multi-x throughput under concurrency versus serialized model.generate(); this is the single biggest serving win and the reason not to serve from Unsloth directly.

Speculative decoding via MTP in Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 GGUFs: multi-token-prediction draft heads now shipped and merged into llama.cpp (May 2026) give ~1.4-2.2x generation speedup with no accuracy loss (dense models like Gemma-4 benefit most, ~1.5-2.2x; MoE less, ~1.15-1.25x). Costs ~2GB extra VRAM; tune --spec-draft-n-max in 1..6.
FlashAttention-2 (attn_implementation='flash_attention_2' / vLLM default) for long-context: fused, memory-efficient attention is essential once context grows on the A6000.

FP8 KV cache (e5m2) on A6000: a MEMORY win only — lets you cache more tokens / longer context, but Ampere has no FP8 compute path so expect zero latency speedup (e4m3 is unsupported on SM 8.6). Use it to push context length, not throughput.
ExLlamaV2 as an alternative serving backend: very fast 4-bit (EXL2) single-GPU inference with low memory overhead; a strong single-box option when vLLM's batching is not needed.

Gemma 4 native function calling vs Gemma 3 prompt engineering: prefer Gemma 4's native tool-call tokens + the dedicated gemma4_tool_parser over Gemma 3's pythonic-list prompt-engineering approach for more reliable structured tool calls — select the parser/template by detected variant at load time.

Whether the padding-side reset bug persists in the latest Unsloth release at deploy time — verify against the pinned version; mitigated entirely by serving through vLLM.
